clusters.title: julieta pin workload and pin check reach a registry and GitHub releases from the config sandbox, but 07 7.5 derives no egress for julieta's own commands and no catalog set holds a registry host.
clusters.scenario: The agent runs julieta pin workload projects/foo.yaml in the config sandbox as J9 says; docker.io is blocked; the operator adds an undocumented allow by hand or moves the pin on the host.
clusters.change: Add to 07 7.5 after step 5: 'The config project's spec carries, in egress.extra, the registry hosts of its workloadRepositories and api.github.com, which julieta pin workload and pin check --workflows read (04 4.3); they are gated like any extra and approved once.' Add those entries to the config project example in 02 2.2 and the words 'its egress.extra holds the registry hosts (07 7.5)' to the J9 workload line.
clusters.cost: Two sentences and two example rows.
clusters.resolution_text: Smaller than a new derived set: the config project's own spec declares the hosts as gated egress.extra, stated once in 07 7.5 and shown in the 02 2.2 example; no new derivation step.

clusters.title: The GitHub rate limit row says the project's github secret covers mise's api.github.com fallback without naming the variable mise reads or how sbx exposes the secret in the sandbox.
clusters.scenario: sbx injects the secret under a name mise does not read; probe B4 with a token fails and the fix is sought in the catalog because 07 7.4 named no mechanism.
clusters.change: Rewrite the 07 7.4 GitHub rate limit row: 'aqua/github downloads fall back to api.github.com; mise reads GITHUB_TOKEN; how sbx exposes the project's github secret (by name) as that variable is a probe fact recorded by B4, which measures behavior with and without it.' L13-23 is listed here for its second half (the 7.4 token path); its first half is R8-07-1.
clusters.resolution_text: Name GITHUB_TOKEN and state the sbx exposure as an open probe fact for B4 rather than asserting a mechanism the spec has not measured.

clusters.title: A tool added on a feature branch hits a blocked host whose quick fix (sbx's native approval) is invisible from romeu, and listing that queue in status sits in a v1.1 bucket with no trigger and no interim.
clusters.scenario: The agent adds aqua:some/cli on feat/x; julieta install fails naming the host; the user must find the sbx prompt alone or merge first, and nothing ever reopens the v1.1 item.
clusters.change: In 07 7.5, replace '(listing the native queue in status is v1.1)' with: 'The error names the host, the sbx command that approves it once for this sandbox, that the approval is lost at recreate, and the durable fix. Listing the native queue in status is deferred (index: Deferred decisions).' Add to J8 one sentence: 'Before the lock merges, egress follows the ref branch, so a new host is approved once through sbx (the install error prints the command).' Delete the v1.1 row of 00 0.5 and give each of its four items a Deferred row with its interim and an observable trigger (for the queue: the first issue reporting a native approval resolved without knowing it existed); merge Q23 into the registry credential row.
clusters.cost: Two sentences in 07 and J8, one error hint, one table row deleted and four added.
clusters.operator_reason: Deleting the v1.1 row of 00 0.5 and re-homing its four items as Deferred rows changes the scope (00 0.5).
clusters.resolution_text: The 07 7.5 and J8 sentences stay inside the spec and can be applied as A; the 00 0.5 part changes the scope, so the operator decides it. Recommend applying both.

clusters.title: romeu parses mise.lock in Go without naming the lock layout it reads or what an unknown layout does, so a relock by a newer mise can fail every sync with no named fix or silently narrow egress.
clusters.scenario: A developer relocks with a mise release that changed the layout; romeu sync fails every project with a parse error naming no tool, and the kit's pinned mise cannot read the lock in the sandbox.
clusters.change: Add to 07 7.5 step 1: 'romeu reads the lock layout written by the mise version pinned in the julieta kit; a lock it cannot parse, or one with an unknown top-level key, is a sync error naming the repo and the fix "relock with julieta lock" (the pinned mise), never a partial read.' Add to the 07 7.3 --check bullet: 'and the lock parses with the pinned mise'. One fixture of the pinned layout backs the parser test.
clusters.cost: Two sentences, one error id, one fixture.
clusters.resolution_text: Tie the supported layout to the kit-pinned mise version instead of a table of measured layouts; an unknown layout is a named sync error with the relock fix.

clusters.title: The environment julieta sets for mise is listed in 04 4.3 and partly repeated in 07 7.3 and 07 7.4, with no single home, so the copies can drift.
clusters.scenario: A PR changes a mise variable in 04 4.3 only; a reader of 07 7.4 implements the driver from its table and misses it.
clusters.change: Make 04 4.3 ('Environment julieta sets for mise calls') the one list; in 07 7.3 and 07 7.4 keep the reason for each setting and replace the variable assignments with a link to 04 4.3. The other lists L3-6 names (git keys, memory layout, ingest commands, reserved names) belong to pages 05, 08, 04, 02 and 03 and are consolidated there.
clusters.resolution_text: For page 07 only: link to the 04 4.3 list instead of repeating values; no generator row, since only julieta's mise driver consumes it.

clusters.title: mise's minisign verification at pin time names no trusted public key, and no CI step re-verifies a pin after it is written, so a hand edit of the sha256 passes tools/ci kits.
clusters.scenario: A hand edit of mise's sha256 in the pin file passes tools/ci kits, which checks only that a sha256sum -c line exists; review of the kits surface is the only guard.
clusters.change: In the 07 7.4 Verification row add: 'against mise's minisign public key committed in the repository (path named in the plan's kit pin task); tools/kitpin commits the signed SHASUMS256.txt and its signature next to the pin.' Add to the kits row of 10 10.2: 'on any change to the pin file, re-verify the committed SHASUMS256.txt signature offline and check the pinned hashes match it.'
clusters.cost: One committed file pair and one offline check.
clusters.resolution_text: Name the committed key and re-run the existing kitpin verification offline in tools/ci kits; no new tool. The pin file is a pin surface, so the implementing diff stays ask-first.

clusters.title: julieta spec validate --catalog exits 1 on a lock host missing from the catalog while 07 7.5 step 3 gates such a host and continues, so the config repo's CI stays red for a case the product accepts.
clusters.scenario: A lock records a host the catalog lacks; romeu sync gates it and the operator approves; validate.yml stays red until a catalog PR.
clusters.change: In 07 7.6 change the validate bullet to: 'lists unknown backend:tool keys and lock hosts missing from the catalog; it exits 1 on an unknown backend:tool only (the case 7.5 step 2 makes a sync error), and reports missing lock hosts as warnings, since 7.5 step 3 gates them.'
clusters.resolution_text: Align validate's exit code with the derivation: an error only where sync errors, a warning where sync gates.

clusters.title: A relock in a worked-on repo, where backend renames and new tools arrive, runs no catalog lookup, so the user first meets the gap as a romeu sync exit 2.
clusters.scenario: mise moves a tool to another backend; the agent relocks and merges; the next romeu sync fails until a catalog release or a gated egress.tools entry.
clusters.change: Add to the 07 7.3 freshness bullet: 'julieta lock --check also looks up each backend:tool in the embedded catalog and warns, naming the two fixes of 7.5 step 2, when one is unknown; it does not fail, since a spec egress.tools entry is a valid fix outside the repo.'
clusters.cost: One sentence; the lookup is the one validate --catalog already uses.
clusters.resolution_text: A warning at commit time from the existing lookup, not a new hook row or a failing check.

clusters.title: Lock-derived artifact hosts reach an sbx policy allow network argv without passing the 03 3.1 domain rule, and no size cap bounds the repository blobs romeu reads on the host.
clusters.scenario: A lock records a host that is a port literal or a leading-dash string and romeu builds an argv with it; or a multi-GiB mise.lock blob is read whole into romeu's memory.
clusters.change: Add to 07 7.5 step 3: 'Each host must pass the extra egress domain rule of 03 3.1; one that fails is a sync error naming the lock entry.' Add to step 1: 'Blobs are read with git cat-file under one size cap shared by every repository blob romeu reads (03 opening, one constant).'
clusters.resolution_text: Reuse the existing domain rule for lock hosts and state one blob cap.

clusters.title: 07 7.3 carries hedges with no trigger: the monorepo.lockfile rule for a mode no v1 repo uses (with a known upstream flip and no check), and locking macOS platforms the product never runs mise on.
clusters.scenario: A repo adopts monorepo mode, omits the setting, and its lock behavior changes silently after a mise bump; meanwhile every lock carries two platforms nothing reads.
clusters.change: Delete the monorepo.lockfile bullet of 07 7.3 and add a Deferred row: 'mise monorepo mode: not used in v1; reopened by the first repo that enables it, which then sets monorepo.lockfile explicitly and gets a --check rule.' Change the first 7.3 bullet to: 'julieta lock passes linux-x64 and linux-arm64; a repo whose CI runs on macOS adds those platforms in its own mise settings, and --check requires only the two linux ones.' The caFile part of L11-22 belongs to page 03.
clusters.cost: One bullet deleted, one rewritten, one Deferred row.
clusters.resolution_text: Delete the monorepo hedge behind a Deferred row with a trigger, and narrow the lock default to the two platforms the sandbox runs.

clusters.title: The GitHub rate limit row hands the project's github secret to mise as a download token without saying it is today the operator's own account token (ADR 0008), so 07 reads it as a download credential where 05 5.4 sees administrator reach.
clusters.scenario: A tool install over an aqua/github backend sends the operator's token toward a redirect host; the row's reader did not know what the token could do.
clusters.change: Append to the 07 7.4 GitHub rate limit row: 'Until the narrowing row of the index fires, that secret is the operator's own token (05 5.4, ADR 0008), so this download path carries its reach.'
clusters.resolution_text: A pointer sentence to the accepted risk; the risk itself is unchanged.

clusters.title: The escape hatches (egress.tools, egress.extra, tool: other, --accept-loss, --overwrite-drift, retire --force) are bounded but never counted, so nothing shows when one has become the main road.
clusters.scenario: After a year every project carries egress.tools overrides and most events say tool: other, so the catalog-gap signal of 13 13.9 is noise and no number says so.
clusters.change: Add to 07 7.5 after step 5 one sentence: 'egress.tools and egress.extra live in projects/*.yaml in the config repo, so their count is read there; v1 adds no counter.' Add a Deferred row 'counting escape hatches (overrides, tool: other, --accept-loss, --overwrite-drift)', reopened by the first catalog release whose diff removes egress.tools entries from two or more projects.
clusters.cost: One sentence and one Deferred row.
clusters.resolution_text: State where the count can be read today and defer the counters with a trigger instead of adding a doctor row and a record field.
